scope: Exact complete 1 Enoch 7:3 source, English and notes a–c only, as a bounded selected Charles 1906 print treatment. No reconstructed archetype, chapter approval, publication approval, human expertise or fresh manuscript collation.

reviews.rationale: Accept this exact corrected payload as a defensible selected-edition treatment. The original Uoft camera and independently rendered pinned PDF agree on the whole two-line unit, including Sat V and Taw VI in the closing word, paired daggers, and star. The English retains the printed connector while disclosing its corruption, renders the toil noun by its directly attested product sense, and maps the inability suffix to the feeding infinitive object without claiming Dillmann col377 directly cites 7:3. All three notes reviewed. No earlier acceptance or release authorization transfers.
reviews.source_review: Printed p16 numbered 3 starts after unit 2 on the first line and ends before 4 on the second. Complete body, same nine words, editorial dagger pair around connector and star before final people noun; superscript apparatus 9–13 omitted from running transcription. Target initial Sat in closing form shares enclosed lower-right counter with same-edition Sat V, not solid terminal of III. Final Taw has crossed stem and no upper loop, matching VI rather than VII. Accept ሴስዮት as printed; no spelling normalized from meaning.
reviews.english_review: Giants from preceding verse are subject of relative opening, rendered standalone as they. Eating/devouring and all the product of people’s toil are present. Daggered connector translates as until without adopting Charles’s conjecture. Inability predicate takes people as subject and feeding as infinitive; its attached plural suffix supplies them as semantic object of feeding. This is a defensible construal, not a claim to exhaustive historical syntax.

explanations_review.assessment: Charles prints the connector between daggers; apparatus11 equates it to Greek ὥστε, calls that corrupt for ὡς δέ and proposes a different Ethiopic reading. The note correctly distinguishes printed wording, critical alternative and absence of a gap.

Opening relative is expressed in standalone English by They and explained. Col1272 explicitly has labore partum with Hen.7,3. Apparatus10 rejects printed form in favor of an Ethiopic rendering of Greek article; preserving all as printed is properly disclosed.

Actual col393 feeding entry cites Hen.7,3. Grammar §125 describes nominal infinitive -ōt/-ō; final -t belongs to nominal ending. Col377 explicitly describes a suffix pronoun referring to the infinitive object attached to the inability verb, but I do not find an explicit Hen.7,3 citation there. The visible Hen.39,14 is in the preceding construction list. The exact note uses col377 only for the general construction and col393 for the direct citation. This supersedes my erroneous attribution of the verse citation to col377 in 03 and earlier freezes; those files remain unchanged.
